notes: Identity independently verified from article title, Nadia Adelina and Gilad Feldman byline, 2021 journal citation (International Review of Social Psychology 34(1):29), and DOI 10.5334/irsp.571 in supplied canonical text. Primary research article (16 pages) with supplementary report, not abstract or secondary summary. No PDF path supplied; no rendering or acquisition performed. Author-mapped replication of original Study 1 hypothesis 1a: social distance (self versus friend), total trait ascriptions versus situational variability; follow-up univariate ANOVA on p.10. Replication pools past, present, and future conditions within each social-distance group, rather than testing a present-only contrast. This design expansion is explicit on p.6; Table 5 and p.10 narrative explicitly map this test to original Study 1. Analytic N: 440 friend participants + 438 self participants = 878 participants, from explicit mutually exclusive final groups attached to the critical test, not from df or generic recruitment N. Random assignment to one of six conditions is described on p.6. Supplement p.33 reports 33 unique exclusions from 911; overlapping criteria counts are English 5, seriousness 11, guessed hypothesis 0, prior exposure 10, incomplete 0, non-US 10. These overlapping counts are not summed. Outliers retained (supplement p.40). Requested test-statistic metric retained as F=9.02; additionally printed Cohen’s f=0.10, CI [0.04, 0.17], is not substituted. The p.9 multivariate social-distance test (F (2, 871)=18.17, p<0.001) additionally includes positive traits and is not the p.10 total-trait-only target. Success coded mixed because authors detect a signal but explicitly call magnitude inconsistent and smaller; effect-specific verdict rather than overall paper verdict. Original side is an unassigned placeholder; do not overwrite prior original fields.
